items.title: Nvidia’s Board Is Weighing Jensen Huang’s Future
items.summary: Mr. Huang has been under scrutiny for an affair with a woman said to be a Chinese spy, as well as for a relationship with an executive at his A.I. chip company.

items.title: Jensen Huang Said to Have Had Relationship With Nvidia Executive Who Reports to Him
items.summary: Mr. Huang, Nvidia’s chief executive, is already facing scrutiny over an affair with a Chinese businesswoman who U.S. intelligence determined was a Chinese spy.

items.title: What to Know About Nvidia’s Investigation of CEO Jensen Huang
items.summary: Nvidia’s board is weighing the future of Jensen Huang, the company’s chief executive, admitted to an affair with a woman who U.S. intelligence says was spying for China.

items.title: Nvidia’s Stock Price Plummets as Board Is Said to Consider Jensen Huang, CEO’s, Future
items.summary: News of the board’s deliberations about Jensen Huang’s job drove Nvidia’s stock down more than 8 percent in after-hours trading.

items.title: Scott Colom, a Democrat, Wins Mississippi Senate Election
items.summary: Mr. Colom, a prosecutor, will be the first Black senator elected from Mississippi since the post-Civil War Reconstruction period.

items.title: Scott Colom Will Be Mississippi’s Third Black Senator. Who Were the First Two?
items.summary: Mr. Revels took his seat two days after Mississippi was readmitted to the union after the Civil War. Mr. Bruce served just before white leaders ushered in the Jim Crow era.

items.title: How The Times Covered Mississippi’s Senate Race, Which Unexpectedly Became a Nail-Biter
items.summary: Three Times journalists break down the twists and turns in a race that captured national attention.

items.title: A Diminished Justice Dept. Braces for Fresh Fights After Midterm Loss
items.summary: The upheaval points to a broader dilemma spurred by the election: whether the department can carry out President Trump’s priorities as career officials eye the exits and senior department officials resign.

items.title: Democrats Face Backlash After Missing Hegseth Impeachment Vote
items.summary: Eleven Democrats were absent, helping Republicans shelve the charges against the defense secretary. It drew sharp criticism a week after the party’s sweeping election victories.

items.title: Tourists Brave a Muddy Jungle Trek to See a Famed World War II Wreck
items.summary: Seven Chinese tourists, a dozen villagers and a couple of journalists forded streams and bushwhacked to the downed plane of Isoroku Yamamoto, the Japanese admiral. Machetes proved handy.

items.title: World's fastest ocean liner is sunk to break another record: largest artificial reef
items.summary: The SS United States broke trans-Atlantic speed records. On Wednesday, it was sunk off the Florida coast and will become a diving destination and home for marine life.

items.title: Democrat Scott Colom wins the closest Senate race in the country
items.summary: Mississippi hadn't elected a Democrat to the U.S. Senate in more than 40 years.

items.title: Democrat Scott Colom wins Mississippi Senate race
items.summary: Democrat Scott Colom has won election to the U.S. Senate in Mississippi, according to a race call by the Associated Press, defeating Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith.

items.title: Why is gasoline suddenly under $4 a gallon?
items.summary: The average price of a gallon of gasoline dipped below $4 this week for the first time in months. Does that mean more relief is coming for drivers?

items.title: Greetings from Senegal, where breakdancers are competing in the Youth Olympics
items.summary: Senegal's breakdancers have been practicing for their country's historic hosting of the Youth Olympic Games this month. It's the first time Africa is hosting an Olympic event.

items.title: Kennedy relatives join the fight against Trump's arch, alleging harm to JFK's grave
items.summary: Nine members of the Kennedy family have joined the legal fight against Trump's D.C. arch, arguing it would disrupt views and cast shadows over their ancestors' graves at Arlington National Cemetery.

items.title: What's behind democratic socialists' historic victories in the midterms?
items.summary: Historian and The New Yorker writer Jill Lepore says the DSA, once maligned, is no longer "beyond the political pale." She discusses the history of socialism in America, and its current resurgence.

items.title: Following big Democratic wins, these swing voters are looking for results
items.summary: For the swing voters NPR is regularly checking in with as part of its Swing Shift series, the election results brought mixed emotions, as does the pending Democratic control of Congress.

items.title: Russia and Ukraine agree to a prisoner exchange as talks end with no big breakthrough
items.summary: Russia and Ukraine have agreed to a large exchange of prisoners of war. U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi led to this decision, marking the biggest humanitarian release since the war began in 2022.

items.title: House effectively ends Hegseth impeachment. And, 3 men accused of plotting U.K. attacks
items.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has been spared from the House's impeachment effort, at least for now. And, federal prosecutors arrested three men accused of being Iran-backed operatives.

items.title: Richard Posner, influential and iconoclastic federal judge, dies at 87
items.summary: He served nearly 36 years on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 7th Circuit in Chicago and was ranked by many as second in influence only to members of the Supreme Court.

items.title: Trump defends his war policies in speech at Arlington National Cemetery
items.summary: President Donald Trump repeated his comparison of the Iran operation with the U.S. wars in Korea, Vietnam, Afghanistan and Iraq.

items.title: Route 66 turns 100. Here are five must-see spots along the road.
items.summary: Photographer Matt McClain shares memorable images from his journey marking the centennial.

items.title: Most transgender people have no regrets years after hormone therapy, study says
items.summary: The study, conducted by researchers in Texas, is the largest yet to examine satisfaction and regret in people who transitioned before they reached adulthood.

items.title: What to do if you, or someone around you, might be having a heart attack
items.summary: Heart attacks are more common in the winter months. Here's how to recognize the symptoms, and the best ways to respond.

items.title: ‘In Flanders Fields’: How a patriotic poem became an anti-war anthem
items.summary: Written by a Canadian soldier early in World War I as a call to arms, it's now often abridged to convey the futility of armed conflict.

items.title: A distress call, a flight tracker and the rush to explain a Learjet crash
items.summary: The fatal accident in Florida last week shows the fallout from a modern flood of data.

items.title: DHS watchdog will probe ICE’s compliance with wearing body cams
items.summary: In several shootings, federal immigration officers were not equipped with body cameras or did not have them turned on.

items.title: Meghan Markle’s estranged father jailed after allegedly removing ankle monitor
items.summary: Thomas Wayne Markle Sr., 82, charged last week with possession of child pornography, had been under house arrest in Lakeland, Florida.

items.title: Supreme Court grapples with arguments over federal agencies’ power to impose fines
items.summary: The case comes as the high court’s conservative majority has pared back the power of federal regulators. But even some conservatives appeared skeptical of going further.
